record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: For private federated learning over streaming, time-series, or dynamically evolving data, how can models be privately updated as new data arrive, how can synthetic data be updated federatedly and privately, and how can private dynamic-database or change-detection techniques be extended to the federated setting?

artifact.category_tag: private federated learning on evolving data
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setting in which a central server coordinates a large number of clients, each of whom holds a local dataset that cannot be shared in raw form. Suppose that each client's data is not fixed but instead arrives as a stream or time series, so that the joint distribution of data across clients is dynamically evolving over time. A learning protocol is required to satisfy a strong notion of privacy, for example user-level (ε, δ)-differential privacy with respect to each client's contribution, possibly under both local and central privacy models, and possibly combined with secure aggregation. Develop algorithms and accompanying theoretical guarantees for the following three problems in this setting:

(1) Private online model updating. Design a federated learning procedure that, given a current global model trained under a differential-privacy guarantee, can incorporate newly arriving data at each client to update the global model while (a) maintaining a prescribed cumulative privacy budget over an unbounded time horizon, (b) controlling the utility loss as a function of stream length and drift, and (c) handling client participation that is itself time-varying.

(2) Private federated synthetic data generation under drift. Design a federated, differentially private protocol that maintains an evolving synthetic dataset (or synthetic data generator) that tracks the changing distribution of client data, so that downstream analytics performed on the synthetic data approximate the same analytics on the true federated data within quantifiable error, while the entire generation and update process satisfies user-level differential privacy.

(3) Private federated change detection and dynamic-database analytics. Extend differentially private change-point detection, monitoring, and dynamic-database query-release techniques (originally developed for a single curator holding a single evolving database) to the federated setting in which the database is partitioned across many clients with heterogeneous local distributions. Provide algorithms and matching upper and lower bounds on detection delay, false-alarm rate, and query-release error as a function of the number of clients, the privacy parameters, and the magnitude of the distributional change.

State and prove utility-privacy trade-offs for each of (1)–(3), and identify the regimes in which federation provides provable improvements over each client running a local private algorithm in isolation.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a programmatic open-problem agenda concerning private federated learning on streaming and evolving data. The combined questions (private online federated updating, federated private synthetic data generation under drift, and federated extensions of private change-detection/dynamic-database techniques) remain active research directions with only partial results on individual sub-problems (e.g., DP-FTRL for online private optimization, DP synthetic data, private change-point detection in the centralized model). No single work resolves the full agenda, so the overall status is open.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems for FL including privacy on evolving and streaming data.
status_evidence.claim: The questions are posed as open problems.
